newsitem.title: USA: Judge says Maryland erred in license tag recall.
newsitem.headline: Judge says Maryland erred in license tag recall.

text.p: A federal judge has issued a restraining order to prevent Maryland state officials from halting sales of license plates with Confederate flags on them or attempting to confiscate them.
U.S. District Court Judge Frederic Smalkin said late Monday that recalling the special license plates was a violation of the right to free speech of the Sons of Confederate Veterans group.
Black political leaders forced the state to call back the plates bearing an image of the Confederate flag, saying that they were a symbol of bigotry and hatred.
The veterans' group, like other organisations, paid the state's Motor Vehicle Administration $15 extra to print the flag and group symbol on 78 plates.
The Rutherford Institute, a Charlottesville, Virginia-based civil liberties organisation, filed suit against Maryland when it ordered the plates to be taken off the market at the end of January.
